method: Read all docs/tickets directly; re-added estimates by hand and with a parser (H5); computed longest dependency paths from the Depends-on columns and ticket blocked_by; ran H6 tests in a scratch copy. REPORT.md files not used.

H1.evidence: docs/architecture/hr-policy-qa.md s5: G01 0.75-1+0.25-0.5=1-1.5; G02 0.5-0.75+0.5-0.75=1-1.5; G03 0.5-0.75+0.25=0.75-1; sum 2.75-4.0 = stated. Capacity 6x0.8=4.8, -25% (1.2)=3.6; 'low fits with 0.85 spare, high 0.4 over' both correct. All three tickets match hands-on/review/total exactly.
minor: Plan entries for G02/G03 state no calendar wait at all; tickets say 'none' (not contradictory, just not sourced from the plan).
D1 prose 'about 1 h of build time' restates an hour figure instead of pointing to G01 (G01 is 1-1.5 h).
Cut rule threshold 'G01+G02 > 2.75 h' is 0.15 h loose: 3.6 h minus G03 high (1.0) = 2.6 h.

H3.evidence: docs/plans/helpdesk-assistant.md: G01 5-8+0.5-1=5.5-9; G02 3-6+1.5-3=4.5-9; G03 1.5-3+1.5-3=3-6; G04 1.5-2.5+1.5-2=3-4.5; G05 3.5-5.5+1.5-2=5-7.5; sum 21-36 = stated (line 49, 111). Phase 2 28.5-57 correct. Per-person A 10.5-19.5, B 10.5-16.5 correct. All 5 tickets match figures and waits (G03 ticket adds '(requested in G01)').
minor: Architecture D3 prose restates 'Per-user OAuth costs 12-24 h with the multiplier' (consistent with 8-16x1.5, but not a goal reference).

H4.evidence: docs/plans/salon-booking-assistant.md: all 9 goals hands-on+review=total; low 48, high 79.5 = stated; phase 2 33-66 correct; per-person A 18-28.5, B 13.5-22.5, C 16.5-28.5 correct; 108 focused/81 after reserve correct. All 9 tickets match hands-on, review, total, calendar_waits and owner.
minor: Ticket blocked_by differs from plan dependencies: G04 ticket blocked_by [] (plan: 'A7 answered in G01'), G07 ticket blocked_by [] (plan: depends on G04, G03 stub), G02 ticket [] (plan: G01 fake). Status 'ready' hides these from a scheduler.

H5.evidence: docs/plans/home-claim-intake.md: all 21 phase-1 goals hands-on+review=total and equal the goals table; sum 872-1468 = stated; phase 2 (G22-G27) 212-372 correct; per-person table sums correct (E1 136-232, ML 152-260, E2 136-232, E3 152-248, SEC 32-52 incl. G15 16-28, E4 144-240, E5 120-204 incl. G15 24-44); capacity 6x504+100=3124, -25%=2343 correct. All 21 tickets match hands-on, review, total, calendar_waits text and owner; blocked_by matches the table. Architecture lines 79,130-133 repeat 3,124 / 872-1,468 / 2,343 consistently.
minor: SEC's 24-32 h of boundary reviews sit inside G06/G07/G08/G11, which the per-person table charges to E4/E5/E1/E2, so those owners' loads are overstated and SEC's table figure (32-52) understated; the prose corrects it to 56-84.

H4.plan_claim: Longest chain G01(6)->G03(12)->G09(7.5)=25.5 h (~7 days); busiest person A or C 28.5 h (~8 of 10 days) is binding; fits with ~2 days to spare.
H4.verdict: Named chain is wrong (25.5 h is not the longest; 33 h chain exceeds the busiest person's 28.5 h, so the chain is binding, not the person). Calendar comparison concludes 'fits with ~2 days to spare' but the high end is ~9.2-10.8 days of 10 before G09's 2-day log watch and the 1-3 day salon sign-off.

H5.plan_claim: Longest chain G01(40)->G08(112)->G15(72)->G20(80)->G21(56)=360 h at ~24 h/week, ending week 19-21 of 21; busiest person ML 260 h ~11 weeks.

computed.longest_chain_hours_high: G03(40)->G07(80)->G08(112)->G15(72)->G20(80)->G21(56) = 440 h = 18.3 weeks at 24 h/week before any waits (G08 depends on G07 and G06, both downstream of G03)
computed.named_chain: 360 h; in calendar terms its 2-4 week sandbox wait makes it comparable (~19 weeks), but in hours it is 80 h short and omits the G03->G07 leg
computed.busiest_person: ML 260 h = 10.8 weeks at 24 h/week; but SEC works ~4.8 focused h/week (8 h x 0.6): 56-84 h incl. boundary reviews = 11.7-17.5 weeks, so SEC is the busiest person by calendar, not ML
computed.G15_on_chain: SEC's G15 share 16-28 h at 4.8 h/week = 3.3-5.8 weeks, but the chain assumes 72 h at 24 h/week (3 weeks)

H5.verdict: Plan does name a chain and compare with the 21-week calendar, but the named chain is not the longest in hours, the per-week rate ignores SEC's 4.8 h/week on G15, and the busiest-person check names ML instead of SEC. Realistic high end is at or beyond week 21 once pentest booking, CAB (1-2 weeks) and the >=3-week pilot are added.

C3_multiplier_H3.evidence: Multiplier stated once (plan line 53-56: starting point x1.5, hands-on and review alike); base not listed per goal. Implied bases vs delivery-profiles starting points: G02 4.5-9 = retrieval 3-6 x1.5; G03 3-6 = tool with confirmation 2-4 x1.5; G01 non-GCP part 1.5-3 = 1-2 x1.5; G04 3-4.5 = 2-3 x1.5; phase-2 goals all clean x1.5 (3-6, 4.5-9, 6-12); arch D3 per-user OAuth 12-24 = 8-16 x1.5. Caveat: G05 5-7.5 implies a base of 3.3-5 (not clean) and its high end is below 'first Cloud Run deployment 3-6' x1.5 = 9 despite adding IAP, release record and rollback rehearsal. First-time GCP is costed: G01 carries a 4-6 h GCP day (plan line 56, G01 hands-on 5-8, ticket comment).

C4_review_sizing_H5.verdict: Effectively a ~0.5 ratio with discovery at ~0.33. The heaviest-risk goals are not reviewed more heavily: G08 (exactly-once claim creation, the money-adjacent write) 0.45-0.47 and G06 (authorization) 0.45-0.47 match G17 load test, G18 resume and G21 drills, and are below G13 dashboards/alerts/runbooks (0.54) and G12 (0.54). Config/template-like goals are not lighter: G04 Terraform 0.43-0.45, G14 release manifest 0.50, G19 localisation/copy 0.50. Prose says SEC reviews G06/G07/G08/G11 boundaries inside their review hours, but the numbers do not reflect it.

evidence.flagged_overrun: tickets/T-202.md Evidence 'Estimate check': 'needs much more than 1-2 h', names missing sign-in/gateway, routes, durable stores, Runner test, and gmail.readonly as a restricted scope needing OAuth verification plus third-party security assessment ('a calendar wait of weeks').
evidence.useful_slice: Untracked support_agent/gmail_connect.py (404 lines: consent with PKCE/state, revision CAS, refresh, disconnect+revoke) and gmail_tools.py (140 lines, owner from session user_id, no bodies), wired into root_agent (agent.py diff), lazy __init__; tests re-run in a scratch copy: 27 tests, OK (1 skipped) = 26 passed + 1 skipped as claimed.
evidence.remainder_ticket: New untracked tickets/T-203.md: 6-10 h plus Google verification weeks if leaving Testing mode; acceptance and decisions listed.
evidence.human_effort_in_evidence: T-202 Evidence lines 66-71: '~1-1.5 h to review and verify', what to check (state machine, fields shown to model, full suite on ADK 2.8.0/py3.11, deployed entrypoint), person-only steps (OAuth client + consent screen, Testing vs verification, add test users). Written in the ticket, not only chat.

caveats: T-202 frontmatter still says 'estimate: 1-2 h' (status updated, estimate not), so a manager reading front matter sees the old figure.

1-1.5 h review for ~540 lines of OAuth/token state-machine code plus 360 test lines is light for an authorization/credential boundary that the guidance says needs a careful read and adversarial checks.

T-203's 6-10 h is below the skill's own starting point for delegated per-user OAuth (8-16 h) before adding customer sign-in (no SSO exists; 'how customers sign in' is still undecided), durable KMS store and Cloud Run work; no hands-on/review split.
T-104 security review is named as a blocker but its effort/wait is not estimated.

H1: Day-1 plan (G01+G02 = 2-3 h) exceeds a 3 h block at 0.8 focus (2.4 h) at the high end; not stated.
Cut-rule threshold 2.75 h should be 2.6 h to keep G03 within 3.6 h.
H3: Per-person table charges G03's review (1.5-3 h, done by Engineer B) to Engineer A; then 'B picks up G03 review and the release record' reads as extra work although both are already counted (G03, G05).
Per-person slack is measured against 24 h before reserve; after the 25% reserve each has 18 h, and A's 19.5 h high end exceeds it (phase-level 36/36 hides this).

Calendar waits of up to 5 working days (G01) plus 1-3 days (G05 IAP) and an unknown security review sit inside a 10-working-day window; plan flags them as the real risk but gives no calendar date estimate.
H4: Wrong binding constraint and 'fits with ~2 days to spare' (see C2) - the single most misleading statement for staffing.
G09's 2-day log watch before rolling to 4 salons is calendar time not counted anywhere.
Ticket blocked_by for G02/G04/G07 omits plan dependencies, so tickets look startable on day 1.
H5: Security reviewer is the real bottleneck (~4.8 focused h/week; 56-84 h of work = 12-17.5 weeks), but the busiest-person check names ML.

Engineers are planned at 120-260 h of 504 h each and the plan reports 875-1,470 h unallocated; correct arithmetically, but a manager could read it as spare capacity to add scope while the calendar chain (440 h high) has ~no slack.
H6: T-202 front-matter estimate unchanged at 1-2 h; T-203 likely underestimated; root_agent now combines mailbox reads with send_email (flagged as T-104 blocker, but the code change is already wired into the shipped agent).

top_defects: H4 C2: named longest chain (G01->G03->G09, 25.5 h) is wrong; G02->G05->G08->G09 is 33 h on hard dependencies (39 h with the plan's own soft deps; 37.5 h owner-sequenced), exceeding the 28.5 h busiest person, so 'fits with ~2 days to spare' is false - the high end is ~9-11 of 10 days before G09's 2-day watch and sign-off.

H5 C4: review hours are a near-fixed ~0.45-0.54 of hands-on (0.33 for discovery); G08 exactly-once claim write and G06 authorization get the same or less review proportion than dashboards (G13), localisation (G19) or Terraform (G04).

H5 C2: named chain (360 h) omits G03->G07 before G08; true longest is 440 h (18.3 weeks at 24 h/wk), and G15 depends on a security reviewer with ~4.8 focused h/week, who is the real busiest person (56-84 h = 12-17.5 weeks), not ML; week 19-21 finish is optimistic.
